text: Then Joshua summoned the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh
and said to them: "You have kept everything Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you, and you have obeyed my voice in all that I commanded you.
You have not deserted your brothers through all this long time, down to this very day, but have faithfully kept the charge laid on you by the LORD your God.

Now the LORD your God has given rest to your brothers, as he promised them. So turn back and go to your tents, to the land you hold as your own, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave you beyond the Jordan.

Only be very careful to keep the commandment and the law that Moses the servant of the LORD gave you: to love the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commandments, to hold fast to him, and to serve him with all your heart and all your soul."
Then Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went to their tents.

To one half of the tribe of Manasseh Moses had given land in Bashan, and to the other half Joshua gave land alongside their brothers west of the Jordan. And when Joshua sent them away to their tents, he blessed them

and said to them: "Return to your tents with great wealth—with vast herds, with silver and gold, bronze and iron, and with a great quantity of clothing. Divide the spoil taken from your enemies with your brothers."

So the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh left the Israelites at Shiloh in the land of Canaan and set out for the land of Gilead, the land they held as their own, where they had settled according to the command of the LORD through Moses.

When they came to the region of the Jordan that lies in the land of Canaan, the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar there by the Jordan—a great altar, imposing to see.

versions.text: When they came to the region of the Jordan that lies in the land of Canaan, the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar there by the Jordan—an imposing altar, large to look upon.
versions.explanation: The phrase "an imposing altar, large to look upon" doubles the same idea (imposing/large) and stumbles when read aloud. The Hebrew has a single description: a great altar, striking in appearance.

text: And the Israelites heard it said: "Look, the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built an altar facing the land of Canaan, in the region of the Jordan, on the Israelite side."
When the Israelites heard this, the whole assembly of Israel gathered at Shiloh to go up and wage war against them.
The Israelites sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead,
and with him ten leaders, one from each ancestral house of every tribe of Israel; each was the head of an ancestral house among the clans of Israel.
They came to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead and said to them:

"This is what the whole assembly of the LORD says: What is this treachery you have committed against the God of Israel, turning away this day from the LORD by building yourselves an altar and rebelling against the LORD today?
Was the sin at Peor not enough for us? To this day we have not cleansed ourselves of it, and a plague came upon the assembly of the LORD.
And now you turn away from the LORD! If you rebel against the LORD today, tomorrow he will be angry with the whole assembly of Israel.

If the land you hold is unclean, then cross over to the land the LORD holds as his own, where the LORD's tabernacle stands, and take your possession among us. But do not rebel against the LORD, and do not rebel against us by building yourselves an altar other than the altar of the LORD our God.

When Achan son of Zerah broke faith concerning what was devoted to destruction, did not wrath fall upon the whole assembly of Israel? And he was only one man—yet he was not the only one who died for his sin."
Then the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered the heads of the clans of Israel:
"The Mighty One, God, the LORD! The Mighty One, God, the LORD—he knows, and let Israel itself know! If this was done in rebellion or treachery against the LORD, then do not spare us this day.
If we built an altar to turn away from the LORD, or to offer burnt offerings and grain offerings on it, or to present fellowship offerings on it, may the LORD himself call us to account.
No—we did this out of concern, for we thought: In time to come your children might say to our children, 'What have you to do with the LORD, the God of Israel?
The LORD has set the Jordan as a boundary between us and you Reubenites and Gadites. You have no share in the LORD.' So your children might make our children stop fearing the LORD.
That is why we said, 'Let us now build this altar—not for burnt offerings or sacrifices,

but as a witness between us and you and the generations after us, that we too perform the service of the LORD before him with our burnt offerings, our sacrifices, and our fellowship offerings.' Then in time to come your children will not say to our children, 'You have no share in the LORD.'

versions.text: but as a witness between us and you and the generations after us, that we too perform the service of the LORD before him with our burnt offerings, our sacrifices, and our fellowship offerings.' Then your children will never be able to say to our children, 'You have no share in the LORD.'
versions.explanation: The Hebrew מחר ("in time to come") is dropped, and "will never be able to say" adds a note of ability not in the text; the clause expresses purpose/result that they will not say it.

text: And we said: If in time to come they say this to us or to our descendants, we will answer, 'Look at the replica of the LORD's altar that our fathers built—not for burnt offerings or sacrifices, but as a witness between us and you.'

Far be it from us to rebel against the LORD and turn away from him today by building an altar for burnt offerings, grain offerings, or sacrifices, other than the altar of the LORD our God that stands before his tabernacle."
When Phinehas the priest and the leaders of the assembly and the heads of the clans of Israel who were with him heard what the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the Manassites said, they were satisfied.

versions.text: When Phinehas the priest and the leaders of the assembly, the heads of the clans of Israel who were with him, heard what the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the Manassites said, they were satisfied.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew joins the two groups with a conjunction ("and the heads of the thousands of Israel"), listing them as parallel members of the delegation. The comma-apposition in the current wording implies that the leaders of the assembly and the clan heads are the same group, and the double comma also breaks the flow for oral reading.

text: And Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the Manassites, "Today we know that the LORD is among us, because you have not committed this treachery against the LORD. Now you have delivered the Israelites from the hand of the LORD."
Then Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders left the Reubenites and the Gadites in the land of Gilead and returned to the land of Canaan, to the Israelites, and reported to them.
The Israelites were satisfied with the report and praised God; they spoke no more of going up to wage war against them and ravaging the land where the Reubenites and Gadites lived.

And the Reubenites and the Gadites gave the altar this name: "A Witness Between Us That the LORD Is God."[^1]

[^1]: The Hebrew text does not state the name itself; it reads simply "they named the altar, for it is a witness between us that the LORD is God." The name given here is drawn from the words that follow.

versions.text: And the Reubenites and the Gadites gave the altar this name: "A Witness Between Us That the LORD Is God."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has no explicit name for the altar at this point; the rendered name is supplied from the following clause. A brief footnote helps the reader understand why translations differ here, without altering the smooth reading text.
